intro: A figure, a word or a number stands just above water. Four answer figures follow; find the one that is its water image. The water image is the object turned upside down: the top and bottom parts swap, while left and right stay where they are and the size does not change.

tips.title: Top and bottom swap, left and right stay
tips.body: Every part moves to the other side of the middle line, the same distance from it: a part at the top comes to the bottom. A part on the left stays on the left, and a part on the right stays on the right.
tips.caption: The flag moves down and hangs upside down; the arrow moves up and now points down. Nothing moves left or right.

tips.title: Water image or mirror image?
tips.body: A mirror on the right swaps left and right; water below swaps top and bottom. So in a water image a word keeps its letter order and each letter is turned upside down, while in a mirror image the order is reversed. An arrow pointing up points down in water, but still points up in a mirror.

tips.title: Every part is turned upside down as well
tips.body: Moving the parts is not enough: each one is turned over too. A triangle pointing up points down, a dot near the top of a shape moves near its bottom, and a line sloping like / slopes like \.

tips.title: Upside down is not a half turn
tips.body: A half turn also swaps left and right; a water image does not. Turned half a turn, 6 reads 9 and b reads q, but in water b looks like p. A common wrong option is the figure turned half a turn, so check that left and right have stayed.

tips.title: Some letters look the same
tips.body: B, C, D, E, H, I, K, O, X and the digits 0, 3 and 8 look the same in water, because their top and bottom halves match. Don't spend time on them; look at the characters that do change, such as A, M, N, R, T, U, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9.
